The two series come from the same projection data (10% dose simulated by the Mayo collection).
Ground glass has much lower contrast with the surrounding lung than a solid nodule: for this reason subsolid nodules are the case in which a very low dose does the most harm. Here they are still visible, but the noise makes the margins grainy and the densest part uncertain.
In subsolid nodules, management depends on the overall size and above all on the solid component and its growth over time. If the noise changes from one exam to the next, the measurement changes too: for follow-up a constant technique is needed (same slice, same kernel, adequate dose) so as not to mistake noise for growth.
